Below it the vertical face runs rows 6-26 (about 21 rows) and carries the white lettering. A grey base sits at rows 27-29. The top band is 4 rows, more than a 1-2 row rim. It sits above an edge line and a tall front face, like the green cabinet reference (top 5 + edge + eave). No side face is drawn, and the width is constant at 14 px.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical brown signboard with the Korean text 카페 in light letters. The sign face has a few brown steps: a lighter edge, a mid face and a dark border. The measured outline is tinted: 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so it reads as a dark brown material tone, not a black sticker line. It has 8 visible tones per 16x16 tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. Shading is simpler than kiosk-a and vending-a, which carry stripes, panels, highlights and small details. The candidate is a thin, simple sign, so I judge density by eye. It sits at the level of the simplest reference, bus-shelter-a, but is a bit flatter than the richer references. The sign face and the pole or base have little grain or highlight work. The text is clear. It would be accepted next to bus-shelter-a, but it is thinner and less textured than kiosk-a and vending-a.

It shows about 8 visible tones per tile, which is above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, the same as the better references, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted dark brown, a dark material tone. The board is a simple, nearly flat panel with little grain or per-area texture, and the lettering is the main detail. surfaces.part: front board face with 카페 lettering

answer.evidence: The top has a lighter band (rows 1-2, #b27361) and a darker band (rows 3-4, #8b4f3f). Both end in a dark 1-row line at row 5 (#533020), and the board face runs from row 6 to row 26 (21 rows) with white lettering. A grey base strip sits at rows 27-30. The top reads as a shallow cap, about 4 rows deep, seen from above, with a clear front edge line. This call is borderline, because the two tones could instead be read as a rim of 2 rows plus a shadow.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown vertical sign panel with a lighter frame edge, a dark base and cream 카페 lettering. Its brown panel has about 4 visible steps (highlight rim, mid, dark, deep), close to the 5-step bus-shelter and kiosk ramps. The outline is a dark brown tone with a visible tint, and the facts agree (0% near-neutral dark edge pixels, like all three references), so this is not a black sticker line. At 8 visible tones per tile it is above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, against 9% for bus-shelter-a, so the panel is not a flat fill; the lettering and frame break it up. By eye it is a little simpler than the kiosk and vending machine, but it is a thin single-panel sign and sits comfortably next to the bus shelter. A careful artist would accept it beside these references.
